newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Monday on last Friday's gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME) with the key September 1997 contract closing above the 24,000-yuan resistance level, traders said.
September was the most actively traded contract, ending at 24,010 yuan ($2,895) per tonne, rising 90 yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 23,950 and hit a high of 24,080 yuan per tonne.
June rose 20 to 23,370, July fell 10 to 23,610, August rose 70 to 23,830, October rose 110 to 24,010 and November gained 60 to 23,960 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 34,540 tonnes from 76,340 tonnes.
Copper opened higher and rose further for most of the session on the back of the LME gains and speculative buying, traders said.
LME copper peaked at $2,530 a tonne last week, and although there was a late Friday upward foray, there was enough profit-taking around to keep a lid on prices.
LME stocks are falling consistently, and on an overall basis are approaching historically, and critically, low levels.
Fundamentals remain strong, with demand good in most regions and new-mined supply not available until later in the year.

World base metal business will be slow to develop this week, with markets closed on Monday in Britain and the United States, but a strong copper market is expected to unfold once more, traders and analysts in London said.
A Shanghai trader said local investors had been inspired by the LME rises, and many believed Shanghai copper would stand above the 24,000-yuan level this week.

"The rise on Monday was also due to speculative buying with hot money (speculative funds) flowing into the copper market from the domestic stock markets, which are falling due to an official crackdown," he added.
Physical prices are at around the 23,300-yuan yuan level in the Shanghai area.
Traders said copper was likely to move around 24,000 yuan in the next few days.
"Volume was thin today although the key contract breached the 24,000-yuan resistance level, indicating many investors are still hayy to stay on the sidelines," a second trader said.
"Domestic hedge selling by producers will also prevent copper from rising too quickly," he added.
Aluminium ended little changed. June did not trade, July closed unchanged at 15,500 and August rose 10 to 15,780 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 150 tonnes from 420 tonnes.
